Row.Text: An early sun shines on the aged politician as he enters Elizabeth's audience chamber. His request is simple - time away from politics to write the history of the era, impartial, without anger or zeal.
The past will inform the future. Grant him his leave.
A public servant's work is never done. Others can write.
History is for the benefit of the public.

On a brisk morning, Elizabeth tours the new harbor, watching the men bundle goods for shipment. They bob politely, steering clear of the queen and her retinue. Though there is little traffic at the docks today, soon it will be the scene of bustle and excitement.
This will be the gateway to the capital.
A foreign envoy disembarks at the harbor, their appreciative gaze fixed in wonder on the capital's beauty. First impressions are key to a beneficial relationship.
Commerce will have its home here.
Merchants are setting up their stalls as the day begins. Fresh fish displayed on one table, imported luxuries on the next. Everywhere, the promise of wealth.
Start a Trade Route and have a Market in {1_capital}.

Letters of poetry lie across Elizabeth’s desk, some in her own writing, others bearing the seal of a foreign leader. The exchange of art is an art all its own, and Elizabeth intends the world to know the excellence of {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} wordplay.
The arts deserve a home of their own.
In the amphitheatre, the {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} bard finishes his performance with a deep bow. The applause from the crowd is deafening.
Place a Specialist on an Amphitheater.
The realm cannot spare coin for frivolity.

What once was a quiet harbor is now a flurry of activity as trade ships wait in line for their turn at the dock and carts heaped with goods rush to the market. Merchants eager to satisfy their many customers complain to Elizabeth that they cannot keep up with demand.
Satisfied customers leave the market carrying parcels of all shapes and sizes. Happy merchants count their coins.
Demand a share of the profits.

Elizabeth’s shelves are lined with the works of the great thinkers, her favorite among them Tacitus, the wise politician of old. His treatises on the workings of government contain ageless truths. Yet few now speak his language, and as time passes, old knowledge is lost.
Translate his work into the modern tongue.
Old tomes are for old scholars.

Where sea meets sky, a row of masts flying foreign flags approach. Ship upon ship sail in a neverending line of wood and iron, their cannons loaded and their men eager to risk life for fame. Elizabeth stands overlooking the sea, a beacon of calm, as her daring admirals plot their move.
{1_reward}, but +3 Maintenance on Light Naval Units.

Before Elizabeth's throne, the charming noble kneels, bent in obeisance and the pretense of guilt. A decade of coy charm spent on the courtship of power only to end up here at the seat of judgment. What good now are your schemes and your gold, former Duke?
Shackles and stone. To the Tower!
Offer mercy in exchange for loyalty.

Courtiers stand hushed as the poet recites his latest verse, but his eyes see only the Queen.[n][n]“Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day? Thou art more lovely and more temperate.”[n][n]A sigh of longing escapes some few lips.
Let me live with some more sweet content.
Or die and so forget what love e’er meant.

The resources of the far continent are in high demand, and Elizabeth senses opportunity. A group of {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} merchants have requested a royal contract to allow them exclusive rights to trade. Such a monopoly would be lucrative, at least for those with means.
We will call it the East India Company.

The sea is a wild place, exempt from the mores of the court, where a clever rogue may wield royal power. Though an enemy may view the {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} privateers as lawless ruffians, Elizabeth sees a pack of loyal hounds.
Knight the captain to reward his daring.

While taking out the laundry for washing, two of Elizabeth’s maids discover a page boy hiding amidst the unmentionables. Shocked at his audacity, their first inclination is to toss him in with the soiled clothing. Some men require firm correction.
Perhaps the river can cleanse his soul.
{1_reward}, but {2_reward} on recently trained Knight in {3_capital}.
Laugh it over by a country fire.

The lands beyond the sea are ripe for settlement, yet full of danger. To Elizabeth’s keen mind, risk is simply a term in profit’s equation. If she doesn’t take advantage of the opportunity, someone else will.
The fledgling colony sits at a crossroads of fate. Pray, Fortune, be kind.
Found a Settlement in Distant Lands.

Elizabeth gazes at the contours of the world map in her chambers. The sea is etched with monsters and waves to signify the unknown. But soon, {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} explorers will see what really lies beyond the shores.
The sea will give up her treasures.

{1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} settlers hurry one way and the next to accomplish all the tasks required of a fledgling town far from the capital. A crier on the corner yells of news fresh off a trade ship - their queen, Elizabeth, desires to learn more about this uncharted land. Fresh commissions for bold explorers.
Send them to settle the continent.
With each new town, the lines of the map become clearer.
Have Founded 3 Settlements in Distant Lands.
Send them to find trading partners.

Elizabeth has always believed that faith is a personal matter, but the priests of the realm feel differently. The queen is more than just her personal beliefs; she has a duty to quell dissent and bind the people with common values.
The {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} people will be united in faith.
Though occasional whispers of old beliefs still surface, Elizabeth is content that the official faith holds sway.
Convert all your Settlements to your Founded Religion.

The ocean is criss-crossed with a steady stream of {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} ships, carrying news, goods, and settlers across the waves. Elizabeth has decreed that no ships return home empty. The new land has treasure, and now it belongs to the crown.
Ours is an empire of wealth.
A line of treasure ships flow into the harbor. Though the periphery may languish, the capital only grows richer.
Trade is the path to riches.

Ships take shape in Elizabeth’s new shipyard, as planks and pitch create impressive vessels bound for the open sea. These are not warships, though - they will be sailed by scrappy and cunning men, tenacious rogues set on plundering wealth from unsuspecting foes.
With fresh letters of marque in hand, Elizabeth’s Sea Dogs set sail.

Despite early struggles to establish a presence in foreign lands, Elizabeth’s colony has prospered. Now, her cities spread the wealth of empire even on distant shores. A tidy return on investment is always worth some risk.
She who controls resources controls the world.
+1 Resource Slot in Distant Lands Settlements.

Elizabeth maintains her regal composure, but inwardly, she feels the excitement of her explorer just as he does. A pristine land full of history, waiting to be uncovered. Discoveries of pasts known and unknown await.
Exploration is the essence of {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} culture.
A curator prepares an exhibit to display the collection of artifacts recently delivered to the capital. A wealth of knowledge taken; a story of empires told.

The clangs and creaks of the factory’s machinery fill Elizabeth with a sense of excitement. Enterprise and industry are the engine of wealth, and the {1_CIVILIZATION_ADJ} empire is poised to exploit the riches of all the world’s resources.
The sound of the factory is the music of wealth.
One after another, factories across the empire churn out wealth to the beat of metal and steam.
